Physical Exam:
Cervical: Facet loading is positive bilaterally. Tenderness over the cervical facet joints.
Lumbar: Facet loading is positive bilaterally. Straight leg raise is negative.
Assessment:
John Sample has cervical facet syndrome and lumbar facet syndrome following motor vehicle accident.
Benefits and alternatives to procedures were discussed as well. All questions were answered.
Plan/Orders:
1. Planned intervention:
-For the patients cervical facet syndrome: Recommend Diagnostic cervical facet medial branch blocks from C3-C5.
The cost of fluoroscopic guided diagnostic cervical facet medial branch block is approximately $10,000.
If the diagnostic injection provides >80% relief, then a thermal radiofrequency ablation ensues with a cost estimate of
approximately $15,000. If performed at an accredited surgical center, the facility fee is between $15,000-20,000.
-For the patients lumbar facet syndrome: Recommend Diagnostic lumbar facet medial branch blocks from L4-S1.

The cost of fluoroscopic guided diagnostic lumbar facet medial branch block is approximately $10,000.
If the diagnostic injection provides >80% relief, then a thermal radiofrequency ablation ensues with a cost estimate of
approximately $15,000. If performed at an accredited surgical center, the facility fee is between $15,000-20,000.
-As an alternative to injection therapy, the patient is also a candidate for 4 sessions of cervical and 4 sessions of
lumbar Biowave percutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (PENS) for amplified pain. Treatment sessions are 30 minutes
each, for a total of 4 treatment sessions per area. Medical expenses are $1500 per treatment session.
-As an alternative to pain management procedures, Intermittent Disc Decompression (IDD) therapy was discussed in
detail with the patient as a conservative approach in the management of the spinal injuries. The protocol treatment
includes 20 sessions of 30 minutes each over the course of six weeks. The estimated cost is $15,000.
